summary: The article traces the history of local special education and inclusive education policies from the 1970s to the anticipated 2025 future, organized in eras. It cites national and international milestones (EHA 1975, Salamanca Statement 1994) and a series of local district policies, each tied to a date and a leader. The arc moves from mainstreaming to full inclusion, technology integration, explicit mandates, neurodiversity and mental health, and finally external partnerships.
one_line: A chronological overview of local special education and inclusive education policies, from 1975 mainstreaming to planned 2025 community partnerships, with named districts and leaders.
key_facts: The Education for All Handicapped Children Act (EHA) of 1975 in the United States later evolved into the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA).

Claybourne County implemented its version of the EHA on September 14, 1982, under Superintendent Elaine Thompson, aiming to mainstream students with special needs and including accessibility modifications and staff training.
The Salamanca Statement of 1994 proposed that regular schools with an inclusive orientation are the most effective means of combating discriminatory attitudes and building an inclusive society.
On September 28, 1996, the Greenville School District adopted a policy placing students with disabilities in general education classrooms whenever possible, led by Dr. Marcus Winfrey.
On October 1, 2008, Rockville Center introduced digital learning tools for students with learning disabilities, championed by tech coordinator Helen Suarez.
On November 15, 2010, the Milton School District mandated Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles in all lesson planning.
On September 3, 2017, the Ashton Board of Education passed a policy making inclusion a core value of all program designs, followed by professional development led by Dr. Beatrice Howell.
The Ashton policy required IEP meetings to discuss social and extracurricular participation and established parent advisory committees.
On September 12, 2023, the Fairmont School District approved funding for neurodiversity awareness training for educators, led by Dr. Julia Mendez, integrating social-emotional learning (SEL).
On January 15, 2024, the New Meadows Education Board required schools to provide mental health days and mental health education, advocated by Dr. Omar Akhtar.
The Brookfield School District plans to implement on September 29, 2025 a not-yet-named partnership with youth and health services for wraparound support, guided by Dr. Rachel Lee.
